capabilities.name: Exquis Layout Model
capabilities.description: Models the 61-key Exquis grid as an alternating 6/5-key hex arrangement and assigns pitch classes from horizontal semitone motion and vertical third motion.
capabilities.userValue: Shows why the same scale in different keys lights a different set of physical buttons.
acceptanceCriteria: renders exactly 61 keys
all keys display note names and octave markers
changing tonic recomputes highlighted keys without reloading

capabilities.name: Scale Path Visualizer
capabilities.description: Highlights in-scale keys and selects a compact practice path for the chosen tonic and scale.
capabilities.userValue: Turns the keyboard lights into a readable practice route rather than a cloud of possible duplicates.
acceptanceCriteria: scale data is sourced from SSLI scales-modes.json
major, minor, pentatonic, chromatic, dorian, mixolydian, and blues scales are available
practice path updates when tonic or scale changes
practice path can be centered around a selected duplicate root note
practice path starts on the selected root and ascends scale degrees to the next octave root
default C-major practice path starts on the centered physical C3 cell and resolves to the virtual C4 octave target
octave labels are derived from chromatic semitone row math with alternating vertical third row starts, not note-name special cases
every physical key matching the selected tonic pitch class is shown as tonic/root-colored, not only the selected practice root
current drill note is visually distinct

capabilities.name: Left-Hand Fingering Overlay
capabilities.description: Overlays left-hand finger numbers using repeatable position-shift strategies instead of piano thumb-under rules.
capabilities.userValue: Gives a concrete starting fingering for one-hand scale practice.
acceptanceCriteria: left-hand mode is the default
left and right hand fingering modes are selectable
4-finger ladder, thumb-assisted, and position-shift strategies are selectable
finger legend remains visible on desktop and mobile widths

capabilities.name: Key Comparison
capabilities.description: Side-by-side ghost overlays showing how C major, F major, D minor, and other keys shift across the Exquis grid.
capabilities.userValue: Makes transposition and duplicate-position choices easier to understand.
acceptanceCriteria: two tonic/scale states can be compared
shared buttons and moved buttons have distinct colors
comparison mode never obscures the current practice path

capabilities.name: Built-In Guide Audio
capabilities.description: Uses self-contained WebAudio guide tones to preview the current drill note or play the whole practice path.
capabilities.userValue: Lets the player hear the intended scale motion without relying on Exquis, Vital, or any external plugin.
acceptanceCriteria: guide audio works without network access
audio status shows whether WebAudio is locked, unavailable, or playing
a dedicated test tone can be triggered before starting a drill
current note can be previewed
full practice path can be played in sequence
at least three guide tone characters are selectable
test tone uses the boosted local output bus and local analyser even when SSLI is available
test tone produces a visibly non-flat waveform and leaves a readable peak trace after playback
preview and path audio can still exercise SSLI one-shot playback

capabilities.name: Web MIDI Feedback
capabilities.description: Requests Web MIDI access, lists every visible MIDI input, lets the user choose an input, and lights the matching virtual key when the player presses a real key.
capabilities.userValue: Turns the exhibit into a self-checking practice coach while making connection failures diagnosable.
acceptanceCriteria: MIDI permission is requested only when user enables it
visible MIDI inputs are listed by name
the selected MIDI input can be changed without reloading
MIDI activity updates immediately on incoming note-on messages
incoming notes highlight virtual keys
incoming notes highlight only keys whose full MIDI note number exactly equals the event, not every matching pitch class across octaves
MIDI touch, hit, and aftertouch feedback never falls back to octave-duplicate pitch-class highlights
wrong-path notes are reported without stopping practice

capabilities.name: Hardware Calibration
capabilities.description: Guides the user through pressing physical Exquis keys so the virtual map can be corrected to match actual MIDI output for the selected layout/key mode.
capabilities.userValue: Turns a useful visualization into a trustworthy fingering teacher for the specific connected controller.
acceptanceCriteria: calibration mode has an explicit UI state
expected note and received MIDI note are shown side by side
calibrated maps can be exported or stored once storage permission is enabled
practice mode can switch between theoretical and calibrated maps

capabilities.name: Practice Coach
capabilities.description: Scores correct and missed physical notes against the current target, tracks streaks, and optionally advances after correct notes.
capabilities.userValue: Supports focused left-hand scale drills without constantly touching the computer.
acceptanceCriteria: correct notes increment score and streak
wrong notes increment misses and reset streak
auto-advance can be toggled
score can be reset by clearing the session

capabilities.name: Responsive Practice Ergonomics
capabilities.description: Prioritizes the playable Exquis surface, keeps required sound controls visible, and fits the main desktop/laptop practice view without page-level scrolling.
capabilities.userValue: Lets the player focus on fingering and touch feedback instead of fighting a diagnostic cockpit.
acceptanceCriteria: desktop and laptop layouts avoid document-level horizontal and vertical scrolling without clipping the right rail
horizontal orientation defaults to the corrected physical-facing view whose rotate button offers Rotate 180
horizontal orientation rotates the physical key shapes rather than transposing upright hexes
desktop layout keeps the practice surface visually dominant
mobile layouts keep controls reachable and make the Exquis surface intentionally pannable
keyboard surface is presented as a controller pad field, not a cartesian background grid
rendered key-field proportions match the tall compact Exquis hardware silhouette
adjacent hex keys use regular-hex honeycomb spacing with shared edges and no geometric gaps or overlap
rotation toggles only between the two visually correct hardware views whose buttons read Rotate 180 and Rotate 0
Exquis key field is visually dominant in the stage panel
Exquis key field scales to available stage space on desktop and after viewport resize without changing the locked hex geometry
practice mode lights two in-scale pads per row, matching the physical Exquis key LEDs without lighting out-of-key notes
hardware-lit scale pads remain visibly lit in both horizontal and vertical practice views
guide tone selection is visually separate from SSLI engine, preset, and FX selection
scale, path, tonic, current, and MIDI touch states are visually distinct
audio preset, FX, and filter controls are visible in the main practice view
all primary sound and practice controls remain visible without document scrolling at laptop size
SSLI presets are selected through engine, category, and preset controls
SSLI engine selection defaults to mature engines only: Subtractive, Physical, and FM, with a Show all opt-in for experimental engines
FX category and FX preset controls appear on the same visual row so the FX chain reads as one grouped decision
when SSLI is available, sound selector engines, categories, and presets are populated from the live SynthLab.presets API rather than the exhibit fallback bundle
selected sound presets are applied through the real SSLI preset/audio API when SSLI is available
SSLI app support files and audio worklet assets are served with the hidden SSLI engine host
selected SSLI engines are initialized before preset playback
selected SSLI presets mutate the actual SSLI instrument type/settings used for playback rather than only changing labels or logs
preset diagnostics intone selected SSLI presets and compare real analyser waveforms, spectrum hashes, engine type, and engine parameter hashes
default exhibit filter and FX controls do not overwrite preset-owned filter/effect settings unless the user explicitly changes those controls
runtime subtractive preset filter cutoff values above the SSLI slider range are normalized before WebAudio playback
physical-model presets preserve their runtime physical settings during preview, including Physical / Plucked / Koto
Physical-model MIDI playback stays on SSLI sustained-note tracking while passing the intended velocity into the physical engine
when Physical-model MIDI playback becomes idle, the physical engine receives all-notes-off cleanup so resonator tails cannot accumulate into noise
Physical-model MIDI pressure uses native model dynamics and does not drive the global SSLI expression filter/gain path
Physical-model MIDI playback uses shaped Exquis note-on velocity instead of forcing every note to maximum velocity, preventing physical triads from overloading
Physical-model MIDI playback uses general independent-voice headroom so simultaneous and sequential notes preserve pitch identity, remain audible, and avoid sustained clipping
Physical-model MIDI behavior must not depend on note names, intervals, preset names, or special-case two-note exceptions
Physical pluck headroom is handled by the general worklet output path without note-name, interval, or preset-specific exceptions
dense Subtractive and FM MIDI playback scales later independent voice velocities and expression gain so six-note poly-aftertouch practice does not overload the synth engine
Physical strike-model MIDI playback receives additional model-specific velocity shaping because struck resonators clip under six-note stress at pluck/bow velocity levels
Physical-model MIDI poly-aftertouch is applied per held note through SSLI physical updateNotePressure and must never be collapsed into a shared global physical pressure value
SSLI physical worklet voices expose independent per-note pressure gain so Exquis pressure changes affect only the matching active note
Plucked physical presets receive bounded per-note pressure through SSLI updateNotePressure rather than an exhibit-side bypass or global expression path
Continuous and plucked physical models both preserve independent note ownership for pressure updates and note-off cleanup
SSLI physical worklet output scales summed polyphony above four active voices so six independent Exquis voices retain headroom instead of pushing the soft clipper continuously
Physical-model per-note pressure updates are rate-limited per held note so dense Exquis aftertouch streams do not overload the physical worklet while zero-pressure release remains immediate
Six-note physical pressure regressions are tested against the actual audible SSLI output using Playwright-driven MIDI and analyser metrics, not only mocked API call counts
Physical-model output must meet measured audible-output and headroom thresholds as held independent voice count changes
SSLI output routing adapters are validated by measured output behavior rather than treated as core sound architecture
one-shot preview and path playback do not force maximum global expression over physical-model presets before triggering the note
low-velocity Exquis note-on messages are promoted to an audible SSLI voice-start velocity
diagnostic console is visible during practice with reset, copy, and exit controls
diagnostic console can capture SSLI audio health snapshots including active oscillators, voice pool stats, active node count, context state, latency, and scope peak
MIDI enablement is the first prominent side-rail action because connecting the Exquis is the first required user step
Exquis MIDI note-on and note-off use SSLI sustained note APIs when SSLI is available
MPE channel reuse releases the prior voice before starting the next note on that channel
MPE same-note retriggers on a new channel release the previous SSLI owner for that exact MIDI note before starting the replacement voice
exact note-on/note-off ownership cleanup is required before the idle all-sustained-notes cleanup failsafe can run
repeated Exquis note-on bursts do not reapply the selected SSLI preset or call stop-all-sustained for every note
stale note-off messages for already-pruned voices are ignored instead of double-stopping voices or clearing current touch state
global SSLI expression follows the strongest currently held Exquis pressure instead of collapsing when one held note reports pressure zero
dense Exquis pressure streams are coalesced so repeated near-identical aftertouch does not flood SSLI expression, logging, or rendering
single-note pressure zero clears expression without falling back to the note-on velocity
SSLI MIDI practice playback normalizes the active instrument volume through SynthLab.audio.setInstrumentVolume when a preset is too quiet
SSLI MIDI practice playback wraps SynthLab.audio.getFinalDestination with a practice output boost so sustained-note voices are audible against the local test tone
when multiple physical cells share an exact MIDI note, MIDI feedback highlights the centered matching cell instead of the first edge duplicate
Exquis channel pressure and aftertouch are mapped to SSLI expression gain and cutoff when SSLI is available
FX chains are selected through category and preset controls
selected FX chains are applied through the real SSLI EffectChain API when SSLI is available
filter type, cutoff, and resonance update the current SSLI instrument filter settings when SSLI is available
verbose diagnostics are demoted from the no-scroll practice view
test tone output is loud enough to be a useful diagnostic reference against the selected synth preset

capabilities.name: Repeatable Preset Sweep
capabilities.description: Provides a Python and Playwright sweep harness that loads the built exhibit, iterates real sound engine/category/preset UI choices, triggers playback, and records pass/fail evidence.
capabilities.userValue: Makes preset compatibility testable across the whole SSLI library without relying on inference or a tiny hand-picked sample.
acceptanceCriteria: sweep runs from the command line against the built public exhibit
sweep serves the built public exhibit over localhost so the hidden SSLI frame remains same-origin
sweep enumerates presets from the live UI controls rather than hard-coded guesses
sweep can filter by engine, category, and preset-name text for targeted regression checks
sweep can restrict to the mature default engines Subtractive, FM, and Physical
sweep can optionally run a one-per-category smoke pass that is not acceptance coverage
full mature-engine acceptance sweeps every live Subtractive, FM, and Physical preset; one-per-category smoke mode must not skip hard presets by preference table
sweep can drive six Exquis-style MIDI notes on independent channels with continuously varying pressure
sweep writes JSON and CSV artifacts with engine, category, preset, status, diagnostic log excerpt, browser errors, SSLI instrument type/settings evidence, and live audio signature evidence
sweep samples the SSLI analyser after playback and records waveform peak/RMS plus spectrum peak/RMS, waveform hash, and spectrum hash so preset output can be compared repeatably
six-note MIDI sweep samples the actual audible SSLI output and fails on silence, engine mismatches, material clipping, or missing voice cleanup
sweep supports an explicit limit for smoke runs while defaulting to full coverage
unit tests verify the sweep harness behavior, documented acceptance command, and JSON/CSV evidence fields are present
